August 4, 2026

Harvard Pilgrim Health Care  
Appeals Department  
[Appeals mailing address or submission address]

Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination  
Member: Emerson Hayes  
Member ID: W807153430  
Plan: Harvard Pilgrim Health Care Commercial/ACA, Massachusetts  
Reference number: POC-9668BA39E4-60948  
Requested service: Knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery  
CPT: 29881  
Surgeon: Marchetti, MD

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the requested knee arthroscopy and meniscus surgery under CPT 29881. The denial states that the submitted clinical records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery.

The available records document extensive conservative treatment:

- I have had 12 months of progressive knee pain that has not improved with rest.
- I used NSAIDs for six months, with inadequate relief.
- I completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy from March 30, 2026, through July 6, 2026. The therapy included quadriceps strengthening and range-of-motion treatment, and I completed 24 visits. These treatments are documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on April 23, 2026. It provided only two weeks of partial relief.

Despite these measures, I continue to have significant symptoms and functional limitations. I experience mechanical locking and giving way, cannot squat or kneel, and am limited to level walking. Examination shows positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.

The MRI dated May 24, 2026, provides an objective explanation for these persistent symptoms. It shows a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking. The articular cartilage is preserved, and the knee has Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1 changes. These findings support a structural meniscal problem causing mechanical symptoms rather than pain that has failed to improve only because of inadequate nonsurgical care.

The records therefore establish:

1. A prolonged history of symptoms lasting approximately 12 months.
2. Failure of six months of NSAID treatment.
3. Failure of a 14-week supervised physical therapy program consisting of 24 completed visits.
4. Only brief and partial benefit from a corticosteroid injection.
5. Persistent locking, giving way, restricted activities, and painful limited motion.
6. MRI-confirmed displaced bucket-handle medial meniscus tear with mechanical locking.

The submitted evidence directly addresses the stated reason for denial. Conservative treatment was not omitted or insufficiently attempted; it was completed over a substantial period and did not resolve the patient’s symptoms. Continuing the same unsuccessful measures is unlikely to correct a displaced meniscal tear producing mechanical locking.

The patient has no active infection or untreated substance use disorder, is a nonsmoker, and has a BMI of 29. These records do not identify a medical contraindication to the requested procedure.

This letter does not quote the plan’s medical policy because the specific policy text, version, effective date, and detailed criteria applied to this request were not provided in the denial materials. Please identify and provide the exact policy or clinical-review criteria used, including the version or effective date, if the appeal is not approved.

Please overturn the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 29881. If additional information is needed, please contact Dr. Marchetti’s office and notify me promptly so that the requested records can be supplied.

Please send the appeal determination and any applicable further appeal rights to me at [member mailing address]. My contact information is [member telephone number] and [member email address].

Sincerely,

Emerson Hayes
